title: Cross-service notice path, merge snapshot home and stale-batch signal are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 052 Notice generation v1 v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 17, 20, 29, 30 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story generates notices inside module P6 and reads v_ace_customer, v_ace_contact, v_ace_account and v_ace_pod directly from the recovery schema, calls CaseWorkflowApi, DocumentHubApi and DecisionLogApi, and holds the merge snapshot beside the notice. In the target P6 rwb-comms owns notice, template and merge_field, P5 rwb-document owns document and the write-once PDF, P7 rwb-decision owns the central ledger, P3 rwb-case owns case, parties and tasks, and P1 rwb-source-data is the only reader of the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and owns the interaction ledger (DP-18). The sources name neither the P1 operation that serves the customer, contact, account and pod facts to P6, nor where the merge snapshot is held, nor how the stale ACE batch in legacy AC7 reaches P6 without a view read, nor which P5 operation stores the generated PDF.
evidence: RWB-E1-052 sections 3, 4 step 4 and step 7, 5 X6, 7 AC7, 11 (DF-ACE-056 to DF-ACE-257), 12 (NoticeApi, CaseWorkflowApi, AceSourceQuery, DocumentHubApi, DecisionLogApi) and 13; Arch v5 slides 14 (P6 IN/OUT), 16 (P5 and P1 contracts), 17 (P6 OUT topic and workflows), 20 (every service writes its own decision record), 29 (one schema and login per service, only P1 reads the views), 30 (ACE Common notification path) and 41 (service catalogue); Ownership Map tables notice, template, merge_field (P6), document (P5), interaction and decision_log_entry (P1/P7), api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} (P6), POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents (P5), GET /data-products/freshness and GET /data-products/{productCode}/records (P1), GET /decision-log (P7); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-18 and DP-19.
proposed: Drive generation through POST /cases/{caseId}/notices on P6, read the ACE facts and the stale-batch signal through P1's published data-product contract, store the PDF through P5, keep the merge snapshot in P6 as references only, and prove the local decision record in P6 and the central entry in P7 within five minutes; keep every legacy value and message unchanged.

title: Review queue operation names, scope source and attach evidence are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 054 Review queue for low confidence documents v1.md (sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 20, 28 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story exposes GET /review-items, GET /document-intake/{intakeId}, POST /document-intake/{intakeId}/resolve, PATCH /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} and POST /documents/{documentId}/review on the monolith base inside module P5, with case lookup through CaseDirectory and scope from the ACE common access check. In the target P5 rwb-document owns the review queue, intake item, document, field and review operations under its own base, P3 rwb-case owns the case read and closed status, P4 rwb-access owns roles, scope and masking, and P7 rwb-decision owns the central ledger that receives the DOCATT decision record. The sources name neither the P3 and P4 operations the suite may call for case status and scope, nor where the labeled example is read, nor how the DOCATT record reaches P7 after the attach.
evidence: RWB-E1-054 sections 3, 4 steps 2, 7 and 8, 7 AC2, AC8, AC16 and AC17, 11, 12 (GET /review-items, GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}, POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve, PATCH /documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}, POST /documents/{documentId}/review, LabeledSetReader) and 13; Arch v5 slides 16 (P5 IN/OUT), 20 (every service), 28 (local record then central ledger) and 41; Ownership Map tables document_intake, document, document_field (P5), recovery_case (P3), role, permission, masking_rule (P4), decision_log_entry (P7), api rows GET /review-items, GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}, POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve, POST /documents/{documentId}/review, PATCH /documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} (P5), GET /cases/{caseId} (P3), GET /me/session (P4), GET /decision-log (P7); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-08, DP-09 and DP-19.
proposed: Keep the queue, resolve, field-review and document-review operations on P5 under /api/recovery/document/v1, read case status through P3 and scope through P4, and prove the attach, its DOCATT decision record and the labeled example end to end; keep every legacy value, message and state unchanged.

title: WIN file path, proof-of-delivery read and interaction ledger home move in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 055 Proof of delivery capture design with WIN v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16, 17, 20, 42, 43 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story runs JOB-10 as a Quartz job at 16:00 inside module P6, builds the INT-14 file itself, calls the P2 integration adapters through WinFileGateway, reads v_ace_pod directly for each business date, writes the interaction ledger through InteractionLedgerApi and has P3 start the notice-period timer from NoticeDelivered. In the target P6 rwb-comms keeps the notice and the dispatch workflow, P2 rwb-integration owns interface_config, file_runs and outbound_item and executes deliverFile on queue rwb-integration, P1 rwb-source-data is the only reader of v_ace_pod and owns the interaction ledger under DP-18, P3 rwb-case owns the timer, and JOB-10 is the Airflow 16:00 file window plus the P6 workflow, not a Quartz job. The sources name neither the P2 operation or event that returns the WIN acknowledgment to P6, nor the P1 operation that serves pod rows and the ledger entry, nor where the REC-05 break list is read in the target.
evidence: RWB-E1-055 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 9, 5 X1, X2, X6, 7 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5 and AC9, 11 (DF-ACE-251 to DF-ACE-258, DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-011), 12 (JOB-10, v_ace_pod read path, WinFileGateway, InteractionLedgerApi, RecoveryDataApi) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (P1 SQL views and contracts), 16 (P2 file contract and P5 document), 17 (P6 OUT NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered), 20, 42 (events 13 to 15), 43 (FileDelivered, FileFailed) and 44 (JOB-10 Airflow file window plus workers); Ownership Map tables interface_config, file_runs, outbound_item (P2), notice (P6), interaction (P1), timer (P3), api rows GET /notices/{noticeId} (P6), GET /admin/outbound-items and GET /admin/scheduled-jobs (P2), GET /data-products/{productCode}/records and GET /data-products/freshness (P1), POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions (P1), GET /cases/{caseId}/timers (P3), GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions (P1); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01, DP-05, DP-09, DP-10, DP-18 and DP-19.
proposed: Run JOB-10 as the Airflow file window plus the P6 NoticeDispatchWorkflow, let P2 deliver the INT-14 file and return the acknowledgment, read pod rows and freshness through P1 and write the letter interaction through P1, and prove the P3 timer from NoticeDelivered; keep every legacy value, barcode, date and message unchanged.

title: Partner eligibility, channel configuration and job monitoring move in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 057 Intake from branches mailroom partner SFTP and email v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 17, 41 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story reads the partner panel table inside module P5, keeps the channel folders and mailboxes in environment properties, runs JOB-12 every 15 minutes as a Spring Batch Quartz job with intakeStep first, and writes the run counts to the job record shown on SCR-44. In the target P5 rwb-document owns document_intake and the intake step, S9 rwb-partner owns the partner and panel rows, P1 rwb-source-data serves the admin job view and the rerun operation, P3 rwb-case owns parameters, and JOB-12 is an event-started step in DocumentIntakeWorkflow with KEDA workers, not a Quartz job. The sources name neither the S9 operation the partner check may call, nor where the channel folders and mailboxes are configured in the target, nor which service serves the job record and the rerun, nor how the Exchange Online mailbox path is reached.
evidence: RWB-E1-057 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 8, 5 X7, X11, 7 AC2, AC3, AC7, AC9 and AC13, 11 (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-005, DF-DOC-046 to DF-DOC-054), 12 (JOB-12 step, POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, PartnerDirectory) and 13; Arch v5 slides 16 (P5 IN DocumentIntakeWorkflow), 17 (S9 IN GET /partners), 41 (service catalogue), 44 (JOB-12 event plus KEDA workers, JOB-11 outbox relay); Ownership Map tables partner, partner_user (S9), document_intake, document_hub_parameter (P5), parameter_catalog, parameter_value (P3), api rows GET /partners (S9), GET /intake-items/{intakeItemId}, GET /documents/{documentId} (P5), GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (P1), GET /me/session (P4); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11 and DP-19.
proposed: Check the partner through S9's partner contract, keep the channel folders and mailboxes as P5 environment properties, read JOB-12 runs and reruns through P1's admin job contract, and prove all four channels through the P5 intake contract and DocumentIntakeWorkflow; keep every legacy parameter, count and message unchanged.

title: Model endpoint path, masking route and agent run evidence are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 058 Agent platform set up E1a v1.md (sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 20, 30 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story calls the INT-23 model endpoint from the P10 model gateway, writes six agent tables in the recovery schema, reads case and document facts through other modules' published interfaces, masks personal fields through the P4 masking service and exposes GET /admin/agent-runs with seven admin endpoints. In the target P10 rwb-agent owns agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation in rwb_agent and runs AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent, P3 rwb-case and P5 rwb-document serve the tool reads, P4 rwb-access owns masking and permissions, and P1 rwb-source-data owns the ACE source data and the data dictionary. The sources name neither the P4 operation that serves masking to P10, nor how another service reaches an agent run through the TE-013 client in the target, nor which agent-run evidence the suite may read without exposing prompt text or model answers, nor whether the live INT-23 endpoint is reachable in SIT.
evidence: RWB-E1-058 sections 3, 4 steps 3 to 10, 5 X1 to X11, 7 AC1 to AC15, 11 (DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-096), 12 (GET /admin/agent-runs, GET and POST /admin/agent-configs, approve, samples, evaluations, AgentOrchestrator, EV-28, INT-23) and 13; Arch v5 slides 16 (P10 IN/OUT and AgentRunWorkflow 60 s then rule result), 20 (every service), 30 (ACE Common masking path), 41 (service catalogue); Ownership Map tables agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation (P10), role, permission, masking_rule (P4), recovery_case (P3), document (P5), sys_fields (P1), api rows GET /admin/agent-runs, GET and POST /admin/agent-configs, POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve, POST /admin/agent-samples, POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations, GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs (P10), GET /cases/{caseId} (P3), GET /documents/{documentId} (P5), GET /me/session (P4); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-08, DP-09, DP-11, DP-19 and DP-20.
proposed: Prove the platform through P10's own admin and run contracts, reach INT-23 only through ModelGatewayClient with a deterministic stub, assert masking on the captured model request, and keep prompt text and model answers out of every response and log; keep every legacy value, status and message unchanged.
